name: Stride Physical Therapy
tagline: One-on-one physical therapy for sore backs, bad knees, stubborn shoulders, and the surgery you just had — with a plan you can see from the first visit.
hours_note: Early and late slots go first — book a week ahead if you can.
license_note: Dana Whitfield, PT, DPT · Licensed physical therapist

rom.label: Range of motion
rom.goal: Goal: 135° — kneeling in the garden again

conditions.examples: Disc pain, sciatica, desk-posture stiffness, headaches that start in the neck
Rotator cuff strain, frozen shoulder, tennis and golfer's elbow
Runner's knee, arthritis, IT band pain, ACL and meniscus injuries
Sprains that keep rolling, plantar fasciitis, Achilles pain
Knee and hip replacements, ACL reconstruction, shoulder repairs, spine surgery
Falls, unsteadiness, getting up from the floor, staying independent

plan.title: Calm it down
plan.body: Settle the pain with hands-on care and gentle movement, so you can sleep, sit, and walk without bracing.

plan.title: Get it moving
plan.body: Win back range, joint by joint — measured every visit, so you can see the degrees come back.

plan.title: Build it strong
plan.body: Progressive loading at the clinic and a short home program, added to only when you're ready.

plan.title: Back to your thing
plan.body: Practice the exact thing you came in for — the run, the lift, the stairs, the grandkids — then graduate.

first_visit.title: We listen
first_visit.body: Where it hurts, when it started, what it stops you doing, and what you want back.

first_visit.title: We measure
first_visit.body: Strength, range, balance, and how you move — numbers we'll check again at every visit.

first_visit.title: We treat
first_visit.body: You leave with less pain today, not just an appointment card.

first_visit.title: You get a plan
first_visit.body: Three or four exercises for home, how often to come in, and when you should feel a difference.

testimonial.quote: I came in unable to go down stairs without holding the rail. Twelve weeks later I ran my first 10K since the surgery. Dana told me exactly what each week was for, and she was right every time.
testimonial.name: Marcus L.

art_direction.identity: A modern, one-on-one physical therapy clinic that feels like a good coach: cool gym-floor canvas, moss-black ink, one bright lime accent, bright natural-light photography of real movement. Confident and athletic, never clinical-blue, never spa-soft.
art_direction.type: Epilogue (semibold, tight tracking) for every heading and big number; Rethink Sans for body and UI. Big, short headlines; comfortable body size; tabular numerals for degrees, times, and prices.
art_direction.color: One accent: lime (bg-primary) for the primary button, the goniometer arc, and the resistance bands. Lime is a fill, never text on the light canvas. Moss-black (bg-secondary) carries the dark bands — the recovery plan and the closing visit section. Everything else is canvas, surface, white cards, ink, and muted text. Never add another color.
art_direction.signature: The recovery plan drawn as four resistance bands — each phase a stretched band that gets longer and deeper in the one lime hue as the load increases (Light, Medium, Heavy, Extra heavy). Also the range-of-motion card in the hero, showing degrees won back. Keep both wherever the design evolves.
art_direction.voice: Plain, specific, encouraging — like a coach who's done this a thousand times. Real numbers (degrees, minutes, weeks), short sentences, no exclamation marks, no 'wellness journey'.
